subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces are local: sets that agree near x have the same approximate tangent spaces at x (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let S, S' ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets (no measurability is assumed), x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and δ > 0 with S ∩ B_δ(x) = S' ∩ B_δ(x), where B_δ(x) is the open ball. If Q is the approximate tangent space of S' at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q: dim Q = n, and ∫_{η_{x,r}(S')} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^n = μHE[n]), then Q is also the approximate tangent space of S at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S S' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → S ∩ ball x δ = S' ∩ ball x δ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 4, (4.1)–(4.2). For f supported in B_R(0) and 0 < r < δ/R, the blow-up η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) meets B_R(0) only in the image of the part of N ∩ W inside B_δ(x). So the integrals of f over η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) and over the blown-up chart piece coincide. Here this is proved for arbitrary sets. The restriction identity of step 3 replaces the parent's use of setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, which needed Borel measurability of η_{x,r}(N ∩ W).
Notation:
- μ := H^n = μHE[n].
- η_r := η_{x,r} (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r), η_r(t) = r^{-1}(t − x).
- For a set T, ∫_T f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against the restricted measure μ⌞T (Lean: ∫ y in T, f y ∂μ). It is defined for every set T.
1. (Dimension.) The first conjunct, dim Q = n, does not involve the set. It holds by the hypothesis on S'.
2. (Support radius.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Its topological support is compact, hence bounded, so there is R₀ with spt f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0). Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. Then spt f ⊆ B_R(0), so f(y) = 0 for every y ∉ B_R(0).
3. (Cut-off of the integral.) For every set T ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_T f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ T} f dμ.
 - f vanishes outside B_R(0), so the integral of f against μ⌞T equals its integral against (μ⌞T)⌞B_R(0) (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, valid for any set and any measure).
 - B_R(0) is open, hence Borel, so (μ⌞T)⌞B_R(0) = μ⌞(B_R(0) ∩ T) (Mathlib Measure.restrict_restrict, which only needs measurability of B_R(0)).
4. (Only the part near x matters.) Let 0 < r < δ/R. For every set T, B_R(0) ∩ η_r(T) = B_R(0) ∩ η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)).
 - ⊇: η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)) ⊆ η_r(T).
 - ⊆: let y = η_r(t) = r^{-1}(t − x) with t ∈ T and |y| < R. Then |t − x| = r|y| < rR < (δ/R)R = δ. So t ∈ T ∩ B_δ(x) and y ∈ η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)).
5. (Equal blown-up integrals.) Let 0 < r < δ/R. By steps 3 and 4 and the hypothesis S ∩ B_δ(x) = S' ∩ B_δ(x):
 ∫_{η_r(S')} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S')} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S' ∩ B_δ(x))} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S ∩ B_δ(x))} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ.
6. (Limit.) δ/R > 0, so the interval (0, δ/R) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of r ↓ 0. Hence r ↦ ∫_{η_r(S')} f dμ and r ↦ ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ agree eventually along r ↓ 0. The first tends to ∫_Q f dμ by the hypothesis on S', so the second does too (Filter.Tendsto.congr').
7. (Conclusion.) f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) was arbitrary. With step 1 this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: The dimension conjunct does not involve the set.
For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) choose R > 0 with spt f ⊆ B_R(0); then ∫_T f dH^n = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ T} f dH^n for every set T (restriction to the Borel ball).
For 0 < r < δ/R, B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(T) = B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(T ∩ B_δ(x)), so the blown-up integrals over S and S' agree.
They agree eventually along r ↓ 0, so the limit ∫_Q f dH^n transfers from S' to S.

audit.reason: The measurable support ball justifies the restriction identities for arbitrary S and S'. For 0 < r < δ/R, the localized blown-up sets coincide, so their integrals agree eventually. This transfers the exact test-function limit while preserving the dimension conjunct, without hidden measurability assumptions.

subproblem.title: A map that is C¹ on an open set agrees near any of its points with a globally C¹ map (bump-function cut-off)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^m be open, let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and let v₀ ∈ V. Then there are a map g : ℝ^m → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^m (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) and a radius ρ > 0 such that the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀). Here ℝ^k = Euclid k with the Euclidean norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → v₀ ∈ V → ∃ (g : Euclid m → Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ ∧ ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ EqOn g ψ (ball v₀ ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. A technical step needed to apply the accepted sibling c1_piece_tangent, which is stated for globally C¹ maps, to the chart ψ of parent step 1, which is C¹ only on the open set V. The parent-supplied proof avoids this step by integrating against the indicator 1_{G_r} of the chart domain (parent steps 4–6). The argument is the standard cut-off by a smooth bump function.
Notation: B_s(c) is the open ball, B̄_s(c) the closed ball, |·| the Euclidean norm.
1. (Room in V.) V is open and v₀ ∈ V, so there is ε > 0 with B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V.
2. (Bump function.) Choose a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^m → ℝ with φ(v) = 1 whenever |v − v₀| ≤ ε/4 and φ(v) = 0 whenever |v − v₀| ≥ ε/2. In Mathlib this is a bump function φ : ContDiffBump v₀ with rIn = ε/4 < rOut = ε/2, available on the inner-product space Euclid m. The three properties are ContDiffBump.contDiff, ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall and ContDiffBump.zero_of_le_dist.
3. (Definition.) Put g(v) := φ(v)·ψ(v) for v ∈ ℝ^m, and ρ := ε/4 > 0. Then B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V.
4. (g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀).) If |v − v₀| < ρ = ε/4, then φ(v) = 1 by step 2, so g(v) = ψ(v).
5. (g is C¹ at every point.) A map is C¹ on ℝ^m iff it is C¹ at every point (Mathlib contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Fix v ∈ ℝ^m.
 (a) Case |v − v₀| < ε. Then v ∈ V by step 1, and V, being open, is a neighbourhood of v. ψ is C¹ on V, hence C¹ at v (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). φ is C^∞, in particular C¹ at v. Hence the product g = φ·ψ of a scalar C¹ function and a vector C¹ function is C¹ at v (ContDiffAt.smul).
 (b) Case |v − v₀| ≥ ε. The set O := {w ∈ ℝ^m : |w − v₀| > ε/2} is open, as the preimage of the open ray (ε/2, ∞) under the continuous map w ↦ |w − v₀|. It contains v, because |v − v₀| ≥ ε > ε/2. For w ∈ O we have φ(w) = 0 by step 2, so g(w) = 0. Thus g coincides with the constant map 0 on a neighbourhood of v. The constant map is C¹, so g is C¹ at v (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
 So g is C¹ at every point, i.e. ContDiff ℝ 1 g.
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–5, 0 < ρ, B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V, g is C¹ on ℝ^m, and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V and a C^∞ bump φ equal to 1 on B̄_{ε/4}(v₀) and to 0 outside B_{ε/2}(v₀).
Put g := φ·ψ and ρ := ε/4; then B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀).
g is C¹ at points of B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V (product of C¹ maps) and at points with |v − v₀| ≥ ε (g = 0 on the open set |w − v₀| > ε/2), hence C¹ on ℝ^m.

audit.reason: The bump construction proves the stated global C¹ extension and equality on the smaller open ball. The two cases cover every point, including the cutoff boundary; arbitrary behavior of ψ outside V is harmless because the product is locally zero there.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent plane of the chart image of a small ball at its centre (parent steps 2 and 4–9)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^m be open, let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and let v₀ ∈ V be a point at which Dψ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ is injective. Then there is ρ > 0 such that the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V and the linear subspace T := range Dψ(v₀) of ℝ^P is the approximate tangent space of the set ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) at the point ψ(v₀) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ(B_ρ(v₀))) (ψ(v₀)) T): dim T = m, and ∫_{η_{ψ(v₀),r}(ψ(B_ρ(v₀)))} f dH^m → ∫_T f dH^m as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^m = μHE[m].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → v₀ ∈ V → Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ v₀) → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V ∧ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ '' ball v₀ ρ) (ψ v₀) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent steps 2 and 4–9, the analytic core of the parent proof, for the chart image of a small ball. It supplies Simon's unproved assertion in the proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 113–126): "since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dH^n = ∫_{T_xN_j} f dH^n".
- Parent steps 4–9 (rescaled area formula, fixed integrable bound, pointwise limit, dominated convergence, linear area formula) are exactly the reviewed and accepted proof of the sibling c1_piece_tangent. That sibling needs a globally C¹ map with a lower Lipschitz bound on a ball.
- The lower Lipschitz bound is parent step 2, (2.1); it is the sibling local_lower_lipschitz.
- The globally C¹ map is supplied by the sibling c1_local_extension.
Notation: A := Dψ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ and T := range A = LinearMap.range A.
1. (Global C¹ extension.) By c1_local_extension, applied to V, ψ and v₀, there are g : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with ContDiff ℝ 1 g and ρ₁ > 0 with B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V and g = ψ on B_{ρ₁}(v₀).
2. (Same value and derivative at v₀.) g(v₀) = ψ(v₀), since v₀ ∈ B_{ρ₁}(v₀). The open ball B_{ρ₁}(v₀) is a neighbourhood of v₀ on which g = ψ. The Fréchet derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the map there (Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so Dg(v₀) = A. In particular Dg(v₀) is injective.
3. (Lower Lipschitz bound; parent step 2.) g is C¹ on ℝ^m and Dg(v₀) is injective. By local_lower_lipschitz, applied to g and v₀, there are δ > 0 and μ > 0 with μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ B_δ(v₀).
4. (Radius.) Put ρ := min(ρ₁, δ) > 0. Then:
- B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V;
- B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_δ(v₀), so μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ B_ρ(v₀);
- v₀ ∈ B_ρ(v₀).
5. (The C¹ piece; parent steps 4–9.) Apply c1_piece_tangent to g, c := v₀, r := ρ, the constant μ > 0 (called m there), and z := v₀ ∈ B_ρ(v₀). It gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (g(B_ρ(v₀))) (g(v₀)) (range Dg(v₀)).
6. (Back to ψ.) g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_{ρ₁}(v₀), so g(B_ρ(v₀)) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)): images of one set under two maps that agree on it (Set.EqOn.image_eq). By step 2, g(v₀) = ψ(v₀) and range Dg(v₀) = range A = T. Substituting into step 5 gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ(B_ρ(v₀))) (ψ(v₀)) T.
7. (Conclusion.) Step 4 gives ρ > 0 and B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V. With step 6 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: c1_local_extension gives a globally C¹ map g and ρ₁ > 0 with g = ψ on B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V; hence g(v₀) = ψ(v₀) and Dg(v₀) = Dψ(v₀) (equal germs).
local_lower_lipschitz gives δ, μ > 0 with μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| on B_δ(v₀); put ρ := min(ρ₁, δ).
c1_piece_tangent at z = v₀ gives the approximate tangent space range Dg(v₀) of g(B_ρ(v₀)) at g(v₀).
Since g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀), this is the approximate tangent space range Dψ(v₀) of ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) at ψ(v₀).

audit.reason: The three declared prerequisites suffice. Equality on a neighborhood identifies values and derivatives, the minimum radius preserves the domain and lower bound, and the accepted C¹-piece theorem transfers through equality of images. The conclusion exactly matches the frozen type.

subproblem.title: Near x = ψ(v₀), the set N ∩ W coincides with the chart image of any open ball around v₀ contained in V (parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, N, W, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^m, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, v₀ ∈ V and ρ > 0. Assume W and W₀ are open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀, ψ(v₀) ∈ W, and the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V. Then there is δ > 0 with (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (N W W₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m) (ρ : ℝ), IsOpen W → IsOpen W₀ → ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W₀ ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W₀, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → v₀ ∈ V → ψ v₀ ∈ W → 0 < ρ → ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ N ∩ W ∩ ball (ψ v₀) δ = ψ '' ball v₀ ρ ∩ ball (ψ v₀) δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 3, (3.1) (localization), together with the inclusion ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ N ∩ W used in the "⊇" half of (4.1). Parent step 3 derives (3.1) from properness and injectivity of the chart by a compactness argument. That argument is the content of the accepted sibling chart_inverse_continuity (ψ^{-1} is continuous at ψ(v₀) along ψ(V); Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2)), which is used here instead.
Notation: x := ψ(v₀); B_s(c) is the open ball; distances are Euclidean.
1. (ψ(V) ⊆ W₀.) ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N ⊆ W₀. Since v₀ ∈ V, x = ψ(v₀) ∈ W₀.
2. (Inverse continuity.) Apply chart_inverse_continuity to V, W₀ (in the role of W there) and ψ, with the point v₀ ∈ V and ε := ρ > 0. Its hypotheses hold: ψ is continuous and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W₀ by step 1, and V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀. It gives δ₁ > 0 such that every v ∈ V with |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| < δ₁ satisfies |v − v₀| < ρ.
3. (Room in W ∩ W₀.) x ∈ W by hypothesis and x ∈ W₀ by step 1. W ∩ W₀ is open, so there is δ₂ > 0 with B_{δ₂}(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀.
4. (Choice of δ.) Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0. Then B_δ(x) ⊆ B_{δ₂}(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀.
5. (⊆.) Let y ∈ N ∩ W with |y − x| < δ. By step 4, y ∈ W₀, so y ∈ W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V): y = ψ(v) for some v ∈ V. Then |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| = |y − x| < δ ≤ δ₁, so |v − v₀| < ρ by step 2, i.e. v ∈ B_ρ(v₀). Hence y ∈ ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x).
6. (⊇.) Let y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B_ρ(v₀) and |y − x| < δ. Since B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V, y ∈ ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, so y ∈ N. Also y ∈ B_δ(x) ⊆ W by step 4. Hence y ∈ (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(x).
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 6, (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(x) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x), with δ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_inverse_continuity (ψ(V) ⊆ W₀, properness, injectivity) gives δ₁ > 0: v ∈ V and |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| < δ₁ imply |v − v₀| < ρ.
Choose δ₂ > 0 with B_{δ₂}(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W ∩ W₀ and put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂).
⊆: a point of N ∩ W ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)) lies in W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V), so it is ψ(v) with v ∈ B_ρ(v₀).
⊇: ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N and B_δ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W.

audit.reason: Every hypothesis required by inverse continuity is supplied. Intersecting its radius with a ball inside W ∩ W₀ proves both set inclusions exactly as stated. Openness of V is neither assumed nor needed.
